Our Seasonal Rate Plan
The Residential Service rate plan is designed for customers who don't mind seas
[DOC 0] https://www.georgiapower.com/residential/rate-plans/residential-service.html
onal price fluctuations in their monthly electric bill and are less inclined to monitor their hourly energy usage in the summer when prices are higher.
Summer Pricing:
Since energy demand is higher during the hot summer months (June – September), generating electricity during this time costs more. The tiered seasonal pricing structure under the Residential Service rate plan is there to ensure the lowest possible price for customers who use less energy.
Winter Pricing:
Because energy is cheaper to generate during the winter months when demand is lower, we can pass those savings on to customers by offering lower rates during this time.

How Residential Service works:
We're always trying to pass along our savings to you, so Winter Pricing under the Residential Service rate reflects how the lesser demand for energy in the winter months makes it cheaper to generate.

Residential Service Disclaimer
How Rate Plans Impact Your
[DOC 0] https://www.georgiapower.com/residential/rate-plans/residential-service.html
 Bill
What you're charged for your energy usage under your rate plan makes up a part of the Current Service charge on your bill. It includes a Basic Service Charge and an Energy Charge, but does not account for things like Fuel Costs or additional taxes and fees.
Learn more about the charges on your bill
How Changes to Rate Plans are Decided
All rate plans are subject to change through our
Regulatory Filings
, including pricing details and payment structures, if approved by the Georgia Public Service Commission.
Please consult the full
Residential Service Tariff Details (PDF)
for all details pertaining to this rate plan.

Find the Right Plan for Your Business
We serve businesses and organizations of all types, categorized primarily by energy size and industry type.
How does Georgia Power classify my business?
We design our 
[DOC 1] https://www.georgiapower.com/business/rate-plans-tariffs.html
plans with different energy needs in mind around 4 possible ways of charging your usage.

Not sure which rate is right for your business?
Try Rate Advisor
Different Plans for Different Usage Patterns
Rate plans are designed around how your business uses energy. Understanding how each rate type works can help you find the best fit for your energy needs and usage patterns.
Energy Only
Simple, usage-based pricing designed for businesses with steady energy use.
Best for smaller, lower-demand operations.
Are Energy Only rates a good fit for my business?
Demand Based
Pricing that includes charges based on your peak electricity demand and overall usage.
Best for businesses with higher energy loads.
Are Demand Based rates a good fit for my business?
Time of Use
Pricing that varies by time of use, with lower rates during off-peak hours.
Best for flexible operating schedules.
Are Time of Usage rates a good fit for my business?
What is the on-peak/off-peak schedule?
Real-Time Pricing
Market-based pricing that changes hourly based on energy supply and demand conditions.
Best for medium and large, energy-intensive facilities.
Are Real-Time Pricing rates a good fit for my business?
Specialized Rate Plans
Outdoor Lighting & Roadway Rate Plans
Lighting solutions for streets, security, and parking areas. Georgia Power offers rate plans and products designed for public and private outdoor spaces to support safety, visibility, and efficiency.

portation infrastructure. Georgia Power offers rate plans designed to support your operational and energy needs.

General FAQs
What electric rate applies to my business in Georgia?
The electric rate that applies to your business in Georgia depends on your monthly energy use (kWh), peak demand (kW), operating hours, and industry type. Small businesses with lower demand typically qualify for General Service rates, while larger operations may qualify for Demand-Based, Time-of-Use, or Real-Time Pricing options.
How is commercial electricity demand calculated?
Commercial electricity demand is typically calculated based on the highest 30-minute average kilowatt (kW) usage recorded during the billing month. Some rates also include seasonal or historical demand provisions that can influence minimum billing demand.
Can my business switch electric rates?
In many cases, businesses can switch electric rates if they meet eligibility requirements. Some rates require minimum contract terms or specific demand thresholds. A review of your usage history and billing profile can help determine whether a different rate structure may be available.
What is the difference between demand and energy charges?
Energy charges are based on the total electricity your business uses during the month (measured in kilowatt-hours, or kWh). Demand charges are based on your highest level of electricity usage at any one time during the billing period (measured in kilowatts, or kW). Even short spikes in usage can affect demand charges.
What is a time-of-use electric rate?
A time-of-use (TOU) electric rate charges different prices depending on when electricity is used. Rates are typically higher during peak demand hours—such as weekday afternoons in summer—and lower during evenings, weekends, and other off-peak periods. Businesses that can shift usage may reduce costs under a TOU rate.
What is real-time pricing?
Real-time pricing (RTP) is a market-based electric rate where the price of electricity changes hourly based on projected supply and demand conditions. Businesses that can actively manage and shift usage in response to hourly price signals may reduce costs under this pricing structure.
How do I find my kW demand or energy usage?
You don’t need to know your exact kW demand to get started—many customers begin by selecting their business type to explore rate options designed for similar energy needs.
If you’d like to find your kW demand, you can typically locate it on your Georgia Power bill. Look for a line labeled
“kW Demand”
or
“Peak Demand,”
which reflects the highest level of electricity your business used during a billing period.
If you’re unsure, you can also:
Use our
Rate Advisor
for guided support
Contact Georgia Power
for help reviewing your account
Understanding your energy usage can help you compare rate options more precisely, but it’s not required to find a plan that fits your business.

Rate Plans With Standard, Usage-Based Pricing
Simple, usage-based pricing designed for businesses with lower-demand operations.

General Service
Most Common
A straightforward rate based primarily on the total electricity your business uses each month. This option offers predictable pricing and is designed for businesses with lower energy demand and steady operations.
Recommended For:
Small businesses with steady usage and minimal peak demand, such as retail shops, restaurants, salons, and small offices.
Eligibility:
Use less than 3,000 kWh monthly
Maximum demand of 30kW
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the General Service rate plan
FlatBill
1-Year Contract pricing
Provides a predictable, fixed monthly payment based on historical usage rather than fluctuating monthly bills. Includes a risk adjustment factor and requires a 12-month contract.
Recommended For:
Small businesses that prefer stable, predictable monthly expenses for budgeting purposes.
Eligibility:
Georgia Power customer at current facility for at least 12 months
Use less than 3,000 kWh monthly
Maximum 30-minute demand of <30kW
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the FlatBill rate plan
Optional General Service
Temporary (<12 months service)
Designed around temporary, seasonal, or alternative service patterns. Offers a higher base service charge and tiered energy pricing structure.
Recommended For:
Businesses with irregular usage patterns, such as seasonal businesses, or businesses with temporary service needs, or operations.
Eligibility:
Service will be less than 12 months
Expected peak demand is less than 100MW
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the Optional General Service rate plan
Unmetered Devices
1-Year Contract pricing
Energy usage is estimated rather than metered.
Recommended For:
Businesses that do not require traditional metering, such as broadcasting facilities, internet service providers, telecommunication, or outdoor surveillance equipment.
Eligibility:
NAICS 515, 517, 518 industries or outdoor surveillance equipment
Use less than 3,000 kWh monthly
Maximum demand of <30kW
View Tariff PDF

Your Bill Explained
FAQs & Helpful Resources
What electric rate does my small business qualify for?
Most small businesses qualify for a General Service rate if they use less than 3,000 kWh per month and have a peak demand under 30 kW. Businesses with higher demand may qualify for Power & Light or Time-of-Use rates.
Can I switch my small business electric rate?
Some rates require a 12-month contract. Eligibility depends on your usage history and demand level. A Rate Advisor or energy specialist can help determine if switching is available.
What is the difference between General Service and Power & Light rates?
General Service rates are primarily based on total energy used (kWh). Power & Light rates include both energy charges and demand charges based on yo
[DOC 2] https://www.georgiapower.com/business/rate-plans-tariffs/small-business-rates.html
ur highest 30-minute usage during the billing period.
What is a demand charge on a business electric bill?
A demand charge is based on the highest level of electricity your business uses at one time (measured in kilowatts, or kW) during the billing month. Even short spikes in usage can affect this portion of your bill.
Visit our interactive 'Your Bill Explained' for more information
What are on-peak and off-peak hours?
On-peak hours are times when electricity demand is highest, typically weekday afternoons in summer months. Off-peak hours include evenings, weekends, and non-summer months when demand is lower.
What is the on-peak/off-peak schedule?

Peak Hours
On-Peak Hours
Occur weekdays, June-September, typically from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m., when demand is at its highest.
Off-Peak Hours
All hours not included in a rate’s on-peak period or super-off peak period, including all weekends, July 4th, and Labor Day.
Is this a good fit for your business?
If your energy use is steady and consistent during regular operating hours, General Service rates may be a good fit for your business.
This rate type works best when your energy demand remains relatively even throughout the day without large spikes.
Typically used by:
Smaller businesses with predictable, lower energy needs.
Is this a good fit for your business?
If your energy demand fluctuates throughout the day or includes periods of high usage, Demand-Based rates may be a good fit for your business.
This rate type accounts for both total energy use and peak demand, making it suitable for operations with varying or equipment-driven loads.
Typically used by:
Businesses with higher or variable energy demands.
Is this a good fit for your business?
If your business uses a lot of energy but can operate more during off-peak hours, Time of Use rates may be a good fit for your business.
This rate type offers lower costs during certain times of day, benefiting businesses with flexible schedules.
Typically used by:
Businesses that can shift energy use to evenings, nights, or weekends.

Best for smaller, lower-demand operations.

Pricing that varies by time of use, with lower rates during off-peak hours.
Best for fle

MOst COmmon

Helping You Optimize Energy Costs in Real-Time
Respond to hourly market price signals and optimize energy costs with a flexible, data-driven pricing plan built for advanced users.
Have Questions
or
Ready to Sign up?
Call
1-888-655-5888
| M-F 8am-6pm
Day Ahead - Real Time Pricing
Provides hourly electricity pricing based on projected day-ahead marginal generation costs. Customers receive price signals in advance and can adjust usage to manage energy costs.
Best For:
Commercial and industrial customers with the ability to actively manage load in response to hourly price signals.
Eligibility:
Monthly peak demand of at least 250 kW
5-year contract term
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the Real-Time Pricing Day Ahead rate plan
Hour Ahead - Real Time Pricing
An advanced real-time pricing option where electricity prices are updated hourly, at least 60 minutes before becoming effective. Designed for customers able to respond quickly to price volatility.
Best For:
Commercial and industrial customers with the ability to actively manage load in response to hourly price signals.
Eligibility:
Monthly peak demand of at least 5,000 kW
5-year contract term
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the Real-time Pricing - Hour Ahead rate plan
Fixed Pricing Alternative
A pricing alternative available to certain legacy customers transitioning from Real-Time Pricing. Offers customer-specific off-peak pricing with a fixed on-peak rate structure.
Best For:
Eligible former RTP customers seeking more price stability while maintaining structured time-based pricing.
Eligibility:
Expected peak of less than 100 MW
Previously served on FPA-3, Part 1 or at least three consecutive years on RTP
View Tariff PDF

Your Bill Explained
FAQs & Helpful Resources
What electric rate does my medium-sized business qualify for ?
Medium-sized businesses typically qualify for Power & Light Medium if their peak demand is between 30 kW and 500 kW. Businesses that can shift usage away from peak hours may also qualify for Time-of-Use rates.
What is the difference between Power & Light and Time-of-Use rates?
Power & Light rates include demand charges based on your highest 30-minute kW during the billing period. Time-of-Use rates charge different prices depending on when electricity is used, with higher rates during peak hours.
How is demand calculated on my business electric bill?
Demand is measured as the highest 30-minute kilowatt (kW) usage during the billing month. Some rates also apply seasonal or ratchet calculations that may affect billing demand.
Visit our interactive 'Your Bill Explained' for more information
What are on-peak, shoulder, and off-peak hours?
On-peak hours are typically weekday afternoons during summer months when electricity demand is highest. Shoulder hours occur just before and after peak periods. Off-peak hours include evenings, weekends, and non-summer months.
What is the on-peak/off-peak schedule?
How long is the contract for medium-sized business rates?
Contract terms vary by rate plan. Power & Light Medium requires a one-year term, while TOU – General Service Demand requires a three-year initial term.

Peak Hours
On-Peak Hours
Occur weekdays, June-September, typically from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m., when demand is at its highest.
Off-Peak Hours
All hours not included in a rate’s on-peak period or super-off peak period, including all weekends, July 4th, and Labor Day.
Super Off-Peak Hours
Only available on our Overnight Advantage plan. They occur overnight from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.
Is this a good fit for your business?
If your business uses a lot of energy and can actively manage or adjust usage based on market conditions, Real-Time Pricing may be a good fit for your business.
This rate type reflects hourly energy prices, offering opportunities to lower costs when prices are lower, while requiring flexibility to respond to price ch

Power & Light Large
MOst COmmon
This is a traditional demand-based rate that includes both energy charges (kWh) and billing demand (kW). Billing demand is based on the highest 30-minute kW measurement, with seasonal demand calculations and ratchet provisions.
Best For:
Large manufacturing facilities, distribution centers, data-intensive operations, hospitals, and industrial campuses with steady, high demand loads.
Eligibility:
Energy demand of 500kW or greater
5-year contract
Not available to customers ≥ 100 MW

Supplier Choice - Time of Use
GEORGIA TERRITORIAL ELECTRIC SERVICE ACT ELIGIBLE CUSTOMERS
A time-of-use (TOU) rate designed for customers eligible under Georgia’s Territorial Electric Service Act or those with very large peak demand. Includes standard TOU pricing and optional flat price or monthly access charge structures tailored to the customer’s load.
Best For:
New customers eligible to choose an electric service provider or businesses with peak demand of 100 MW or greater seeking customized pricing structures.
Eligibility:
New customers eligible under the Georgia Territorial Electric Service Act
Variable contract terms, typically 3-year term
Service at one standard voltage

Day Ahead - Real Time Pricing
Provides hourly electricity pricing based on projected day-ahead marginal generation costs. Customers receive price signals in advance and can adjust usage to manage energy costs.
Best For:
Commercial and industrial customers with the ability to actively manage load in response to hourly price signals.
Eligibility:
Monthly peak demand of at least 250 kW
5-year contract term
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the Real-Time Pricing Day Ahead rate plan
Hour Ahead - Real Time Pricing
Provides electricity pricing updated hourly, at least 60 minutes before becoming effective. Designed for customers able to respond quickly to price volatility.
Best For:
Commercial and industrial customers with the ability to actively manage load in response to hourly price signals.
Eligibility:
Monthly peak demand of at least 5,000 kW
5-year contract term
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the Real-time Pricing - Hour Ahead rate plan

Price Protection Products
FOR CUSTOMERS SEEKING PRICE PROTECTION

Best For:
RTP customers seeking to hedge against hourly price volatility while maintaining operational flexibility.
Eligibility:
Must be billed on hourly RTP pricing
Purchase amounts determined based on historical usage

View Tariff Details for the Price Protection Products rate plan

marginally priced

Your Bill Explained
FAQs & Helpful Resources
What electric rate applies to large industrial customers?
Businesses with peak demand of 500 kW or greater typically qualify for Power & Light Large or specific Time-of-Use rates depending on load profile and eligibility.
What is the difference between Power & Light and Time-of-Use rates?
Power & Light Large is primarily demand-based with tiered energy pricing. Time-of-Use rates vary pricing by time of day and may reward businesses that can shift energy use outside peak summer hours.
How is billing demand calculated for large commercial customers?
Billing demand is based on the highest 30-minute kW measurement during the billing month, and may include seasonal ratchet provisions depending on the tariff.
What is a demand ratchet?
A demand ratchet uses your highest historical peak demand to establish a minimum billing demand for future months, particularly during seasonal periods.
What is load factor and why does it matter?
Load factor measures how consistently electricity is used compared to peak demand. A higher load factor indicates more efficient use of energy and may qualify customers for specific rate plans such as Time of Use - High Load Factor.
How long is the contract for large commercial or industrial business rates?
Contract terms vary by rate plan. Power & Light Large requires a five-year term, while Time of Use rates requires a one-year initial term.

School Service
Demand-based
A full-use electric rate designed specifically for academic institutions, featuring tiered energy pricing with demand charges structured around school operating patterns.
Best For:
Public and private elementary, middle, high schools, and colleges operating under a single delivery point.
Eligibility:
1-year contract for ≤500 kW, 5-years contract for >500 kW
Public or private academic institutions
Regular instructional programs conducted
Single delivery point through a single meter
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the School Service rate plan
School Load Management
Demand-Based with Load Management
A demand-based rate that encourages schools to manage and shift electricity use during peak summer periods through defined load-management pricing structures.
Best For:
Newly constructed or reconstructed academic facilities
Eligibility:
5-year contract
Public or private academic institutions
Newly constructed or reconstructed buildings
Single delivery point
Minimum billing demand thresholds apply
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the School Load Management rate plan

Try Rate Advisor
Frequently Asked Questions
Get all the details by reading common questions and answers.
How are demand charges calculated for schools?
Demand charges are typically based on the highest 30-minute kilowatt (kW) usage during the billing month. Some governmental rates also include seasonal or historical demand calculations that affect minimum billing demand.
What electric rate do schools qualify for in Georgia?
Public and private academic institutions in Georgia may qualify for School Service or School Load Management rates, depending on building type, demand level, and operational structure. Eligibility typically requires service through a single delivery point and meter.
What is the difference between School Service and School Load Management?
School Service is a full-use demand-based rate for academic institutions, while School Load Management is designed for newly constructed or reconstructed school buildings that actively manage peak summer electricity demand.

Government Facilities
Outdoor Lighting
Traffic Control
A rate for large federal, state, and municipal agencies operating substantial facilities.
Full Use Service to Governmental Institutions
demand-based
A large-load demand-based rate for federal, state, and municipal agencies operating substantial facilities through a single meter.
Best For:
Large government campuses, agencies, or institutional facilities with significant and consistent demand.
Eligibility:
1-year contract
Federal, state, or local government agencies
Single delivery point through a single meter
Not available for predominantly residential facilities
Not available to network underground or service below 12 kV after Dec. 29, 1981
Minimum demand thresholds apply (3,000–6,000 kW depending on application date)
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the Full Use Service to Governmental Institutions rate plan
Rates for government-operated outdoor lighting, including streets, roadways, public spaces, and facilities.
Outdoor Lighting Service – Governmental
for government agencies
Designed for outdoor lighting service for federal, state, and local government agencies, including streets, public spaces, and facilities.
Best For:
Municipalities and public agencies requiring company-owned and maintained lighting infrastructure.
Eligibility:
Federal, State, or Local Government agencies
5-year contract
Energy billed under EOL tariff. See tarrif details.

View Tariff Details for the Outdoor Lighting – Governmental rate plan
Rates for government-operated traffic control and public infrastructure systems.
Traffic Control – Metered
energy based
An energy-based rate for metered municipal traffic control equipment, including signals, cameras, and related infrastructure located on public streets and highways.
Best For:
Municipal traffic signals, cameras, and related equipment
Eligibility:
1-year contract term
Traffic control equipment owned and operated by a municipality or government agency
Located on public streets or highways
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the Traffic Control – Metered rate plan
Traffic Control – Unmetered
Fixed Device-Based
A fixed, device-based rate for unmetered traffic control equipment such as traffic signals, school flashers and traffic flashers.
Best For:
Municipalities operating unmetered traffic signal devices.
Eligibility:
1-year contract term
Not avaliable for new premises
Government-owned traffic control devices
Located on public streets or highways
View Tariff PDF
View Tariff Details for the Traffic Control – Unmetered rate plan

Frequently Asked Questions
Get all the details by reading common questions and answers.
What rate applies to government agencies or municipal facilities?
Large federal, state, and local government agencies operating through a single delivery point may qualify for Full Use Service to Governmental Institutions, which includes structured demand and energy pricing.
Do traffic signals and municipal infrastructure qualify for special electric rates?
Yes. Municipal traffic control systems may qualify for either Metered Traffic Control Service or Unmetered Traffic Control Service, depending on how the equipment is installed and billed.
How are demand charges calculated for government facilities?
Demand charges are typically based on the highest 30-minute kilowatt (kW) usage during the billing month. Some governmental rates also include seasonal or historical demand calculations that affect minimum billing demand.
